I'm 76 years old. I've been farming these fields for 50 years — longer than most folks around here have been alive. Me and my old lady, just the two of us now on 4.1 mu. We're small, cash is always tight, but I know every inch of this land. At my age, I don't gamble on new tricks. I stick with what works, and I sleep fine at night.

I've got 3 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, and about 1 mu of cotton on the side. I used to grow more cotton, but picking it kills my back nowadays, so I've shrunk it down over the years.

**Winter wheat** went in last October, same as always. Local variety — I save seed some years, buy it others. Before planting I put down base fertilizer: about 10 kg of urea per mu plus some compound fertilizer. Now it's spring, and I'll topdress at jointing with another 5 kg N per mu. Three irrigations total: green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Pumping water isn't cheap — the meter runs fast — but dry wheat means no harvest, and I can't afford a total loss. I spray for weeds and aphids if I see them. I expect about 400 kg/mu. I'm not chasing records anymore; I want steady, reliable grain.

**Summer maize** goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June. That window is brutal — sometimes only five or six days. I buy hybrid seed, about 55 yuan per mu. It's more expensive than keeping my own, but the yield difference pays for itself. I put down about 12 kg N per mu at planting, all at once — no time for splitting in this system. Maybe one irrigation in July if the heat is bad and it hasn't rained. Maize usually gives me around 450 kg/mu if the weather cooperates.

**Cotton** gets planted in late April. I plow that patch good in spring. I use less fertilizer than wheat — about 10 kg N per mu total, one application at planting. Two irrigations, one in June and one in August if needed. Cotton needs insecticide — those bollworms will ruin you if you let them. Yield should be around 260 kg/mu of seed cotton. The problem is picking. I hire labor for that now; my back won't handle bending over for days anymore. Costs me, but what choice do I have?

Total input costs this year — seed, fertilizer, pumping, pesticides, hired help for harvest — will run me about 1,600 yuan. That's a lot for us. But if I skimp on fertilizer or irrigation and the crop fails, we're in real trouble. Better to spend a bit more and sleep easy.
